chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Anbasa Al-Aabid, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If you do not have weeping, then pretend to weep.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.بُكَاءٌ: Weeping, crying (specifically in a religious or emotional context)
key_terms.فَتَبَاكَ: Then pretend/feign (imperative form from the root B-K-Y)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by 'pretend to weep' if you cannot weep naturally?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) encourages the deliberate cultivation of tears, even if they do not come naturally, highlighting the Shia scholarly view that physical manifestation of sorrow often precedes and deepens spiritual humility. This practice is seen as a means to soften the heart and enhance khushu' (presence of heart) during worship, reflecting the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt who frequently wept upon reciting the Quran. By actively inducing weeping, the believer aligns their physical state with their inner devotion, fostering a deeper connection with the Divine.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Anbasa Al Aabid who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you cannot be with the weeping, so pretend (try) to weep’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Anbasah al-‘Abid who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘If you cannot weep then make a weeping-like face.’”
